description:
Vital Recorder is open on the Windows desktop. Three real intraoperative vital signs recordings are available in C:\Users\Docker\Desktop\VitalRecorderData\: 0001.vital (~3h 12min), 0002.vital (~4h 22min), and 0003.vital (~1h 13min).

You are a clinical researcher studying perioperative time management and surgical workflow efficiency. Your task is to analyze the temporal structure of the longest case in the dataset.

You must:
1. Open each recording to determine which case has the longest total duration.
2. For the longest case, navigate to its event markers to identify the exact perioperative phases: the pre-operative period (case start to surgery start), the intraoperative period (surgery start to surgery end), and the post-operative/emergence period (surgery end to case end).
3. Export the intraoperative segment only (from Surgery started to Surgery finished) from the longest case to a CSV file saved as C:\Users\Docker\Desktop\longest_case_intraop.csv.
4. Produce a written phase analysis report saved as C:\Users\Docker\Desktop\phase_analysis.txt that documents: the case identifier, total recording duration, the duration of each perioperative phase in minutes, the percentage of total time each phase represents, and the physiological tracks available in that case.

Login: Windows Desktop user (no Vital Recorder login required). All vital data files are in C:\Users\Docker\Desktop\VitalRecorderData\.
